name: Mexico (federal)
note: Death registration is state law in Mexico; this file uses the Código Civil Federal (arts. 117–129) as the reference model, together with federal health, population, electoral, tax and social-security law. A physician issues the federal certificado de defunción, the occupants or institution must notify the civil registrar within 24 hours, and the registrar authorises burial. Registries feed the Registro Nacional de Población by agreement and must notify the INE within ten days; IMSS and the SAT learn mainly from the family.

steps.title: Physician establishes the death
steps.who: A medical practitioner legally authorised to practise (médico legalmente autorizado), or another person the health authority authorises.
steps.summary: The Juez del Registro Civil must satisfy himself of the death through a certificate from a licensed physician before authorising burial; the Ley General de Salud makes the death certificate a federal sanitary certificate.

steps.title: Physician issues the certificado de defunción with the cause
steps.who: Medical professionals or persons authorised by the competent health authority, on the Secretaría de Salud's approved model form.
steps.trigger: Death confirmed and its causes determined.
steps.summary: The certificado de defunción is issued once death is confirmed and the causes determined, on the federal model form; the Secretaría de Salud distributes the forms and organises capture and exchange of the data.

steps.title: Notify the Juez del Registro Civil within 24 hours
steps.localName: aviso de fallecimiento / acta de defunción
steps.who: Those living in the house where the death occurred; directors or administrators of prisons, hospitals, schools or other communal houses; hotel and boarding-house guests.
steps.summary: Under the federal model code the occupants of the house, or the head of the institution, must notify the civil registrar within 24 hours, on pain of a fine of 500 to 5,000 pesos. The acta records the declaration and is signed by two witnesses, relatives preferred. Each state's civil code governs in practice.

steps.title: Hospital or institution notifies the registrar
steps.who: Directors or administrators of hospitals, prisons, schools or other communal establishments.
steps.summary: The same 24-hour duty applies to heads of institutions for deaths occurring in them.

steps.title: Municipal authority certifies a death where there is no registry office
steps.who: The municipal authority of the place.
steps.trigger: A death in a place without a Registro Civil office.
steps.summary: The municipal authority issues a constancia and sends it to the competent registrar, who draws up the acta.

steps.title: Registrar refers a suspected violent death to the Ministerio Público
steps.who: The Juez del Registro Civil; the Ministerio Público (public prosecutor) investigates.
steps.trigger: The registrar suspects the death was violent.
steps.summary: The registrar reports to the Ministerio Público with all information held; when the Ministerio Público investigates a death it tells the registrar so the acta can be entered.

steps.title: Registrar authorises burial or cremation
steps.trigger: Registration on the basis of the medical certificate.
steps.summary: No burial or cremation without the registrar's written authorisation, and not before 24 hours have passed since the death unless the competent authority orders otherwise.

steps.title: Certified copy to the registrar of the domicile
steps.who: The registrar of the place of death to the registrar of the deceased's domicile.
steps.summary: A certified copy of the acta is sent to the registrar of the domicile to be entered there too.

steps.title: Copies of the acta de defunción
steps.localName: copia certificada del acta de defunción
steps.who: Any person may request a testimonio (certified copy); registrars must issue it.
steps.summary: The federal model code makes acts of the civil registry open: anyone may ask for a copy and the registrar is bound to give it.

steps.title: Civil registries feed deaths to the Registro Nacional de Población
steps.who: State civil registries under convenios with the Secretaría de Gobernación (RENAPO).
steps.latencyNote: mantener permanentemente actualizado; sin plazo (lgp-93; Reglamento LGP leído)
steps.summary: The Secretaría de Gobernación signs agreements with local authorities to collect births, disability and deaths so the Registro Nacional de Población, keyed on the CURP, stays permanently updated. The law does not set a deadline; the mechanism is by agreement.

steps.title: Registrar informs the INE; deceased removed from the Padrón Electoral
steps.who: Civil registry officials, to the Instituto Nacional Electoral (Dirección Ejecutiva del Registro Federal de Electores).
steps.trigger: Issue of the acta de defunción.

deadline.text: within ten days of issue of the acta

steps.summary: Registry officials must report deaths of citizens to the INE within ten days of issuing the acta, and the deceased are removed from the electoral roll.

steps.title: Death-certificate data captured by the health system
steps.who: Secretaría de Salud, state governments and state health services.
steps.trigger: Issue of the certificado de defunción.
steps.summary: The Ley General de Salud requires the health authorities to capture, generate and exchange the information from death certificates; this is the mortality-statistics route. The INEGI leg was not sourced.

steps.title: SAT cancels the RFC; heirs revoke the e.firma
steps.who: The SAT, on information in its systems or from other authorities; a legally authorised third party for the e.firma.
steps.trigger: The death becomes known to the SAT.
steps.summary: The SAT may cancel the taxpayer registration (RFC) of a deceased individual. Revocation of the deceased's e.firma certificate must be requested by an authorised third party who attaches the acta de defunción.

steps.title: Family claims IMSS funeral aid with the acta
steps.who: The person, preferably a relative, who paid for the funeral of an insured person or pensioner.
steps.trigger: The death of an IMSS-insured person or pensioner.
steps.summary: IMSS learns of the death when a relative claims the funeral grant by presenting a copy of the acta de defunción; no statutory feed from the civil registry to IMSS or ISSSTE was found.

steps.title: Private bodies validate CURPs against the national identity platform
steps.who: Any public or private entity; the RENAPO Plataforma Única de Identidad.
steps.trigger: A private entity providing a service needs to identify a person.
steps.summary: Since July 2025 every public or private entity must request the CURP, and the RNP runs a platform for consulting and validating CURPs. The law does not say whether the platform returns death status; that part is unverified.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Federal model (Código Civil Federal): notice within 24 hours. Registration is state law; each state's civil code sets its own deadline.

informantDuty.note: Occupants of the house, heads of hospitals, prisons and other institutions, and hotel guests all carry the duty; witnesses are preferably relatives.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of certificates; the registrar refers suspected violent deaths to the Ministerio Público.

electronicRegistration.note: The federal model code still prescribes typed entries in triplicate on special forms; the states have their own (largely digitised) systems, which were not examined.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Registro Nacional de Población (CURP)
centralPopulationRegister.note: Registro Nacional de Población (RENAPO, Secretaría de Gobernación), keyed on the CURP and fed with deaths by state registries under convenios.

governmentPropagation.note: Registries feed RENAPO (by agreement) and must tell the INE within 10 days, but IMSS learns from the family's funeral-aid claim and the SAT acts on its own information or the heirs' request; no single feed to benefits bodies was sourced.

certificateAccess.note: Federal model: anyone may ask for a copy of a civil registry act.

privateSectorVerification.note: Private entities must collect the CURP and RENAPO runs a CURP consultation/validation platform; whether it shows death status is not stated in law.

gaps: Registration is governed by 32 state civil codes and registry laws; only the Código Civil Federal model was read. State deadlines, electronic registration and certificate-access rules vary and were not checked.
No statutory feed from civil registries to IMSS or ISSSTE was found; IMSS learns of deaths through benefit claims (LSS art. 104). ISSSTE law not read.

The mechanism by which the SAT learns of deaths for RFC cancellation (CFF art. 27 C XIII) is not stated in the law; the Reglamento del CFF could not be fetched (diputados.gob.mx regley path returned 404).
Whether RENAPO's Plataforma Única de Identidad / CURP consultation exposes death status ("baja por defunción") to private entities is not stated in the LGP; RENAPO guidance on gob.mx was not checked.
The INEGI mortality-statistics route (Ley del Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica) was not sourced.
